text: It is in this spirit that I wish to state my considered position on the Motion.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I do not disagree with the principles in paragraphs 1 and 6 of the Motion.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Honesty and integrity are indeed the fundamental pillars of our Parliamentary and political system.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Every MP has a solemn duty to respect the law and honour the trust placed in them by Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Regardless of the differing views in this House on Ms Lim and Mr Faisal, it is important that Parliament does not allow this to drag on for too long.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The Leader has said that Parliament will separately consider the matter on another occasion.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I trust that it is not the intention of the Government to let this matter persist over the next few years as having the Sword of Damocles hanging over their heads would be unfair to them.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Paragraphs 2, 3 and 4 pertain to Mr Pritam Singh.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: As Mr Pritam Singh has stated today, he maintains that he disagrees with the judgment of the Court and the findings of the COP.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I note that in 2022, Parliament chose to refer Mr Singh to the PP.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: After a lengthy investigation, a trial and an appeal, the legal process has concluded.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Mr Singh has been sentenced and has paid his fines.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: We must also remember that the position of the Leader of the Opposition remains a role constituted at the Prime Minister's prerogative.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: If the Prime Minister now deems the appointment untenable, he has the authority to rescind it.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The Leader said MPs are entitled to express their view on Mr Singh's suitability for that role.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Is the Prime Minister seeking the views of Parliament to make his executive decision?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The outcome of this Motion may be a foregone conclusion due to the mathematical reality of this House, but the moral weight of the decision rests on every Member.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Regardless of Parliament's decision, the WP will continue our work on the ground.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: We will let our commitment and our service to our constituents speak for themselves.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Ultimately, it is for the voters to decide on the representatives they want serving them.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: In recent weeks, I have been heartened by the many residents I have met during house visits and at neighbourhood coffee shops.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Many have offered words of encouragement and concern and have reaffirmed their support for us through this episode.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: They have urged us to stay focused on the issues that matter to their families and their livelihoods.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I express my heartfelt thanks to our residents and supporters.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Their trust is a reminder of why we are here and why we must press on with our responsibilities to our residents and the nation.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Once this Motion is settled, I hope this House can move on to the crucial matters that affect the lives of all Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I am an engineer, so, I will be very short and sharp.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I am also a fellow and a former vice president of the Institution of Engineers.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: We are trained to analyse systematically and logically.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Interestingly, I am also a layperson of the investigation and disciplinary panel of the Institute of Singapore Chartered Accountants.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: We take our roles very seriously as they have impact on a person's reputation and also his livelihood.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: We rely on objective evidence and less on emotions or personal opinions.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I am going to ask three questions to myself in order to resolve or understand how I react to this Motion: principle, facts and action.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: This Motion is all about honesty and integrity so that we have built trust in this august Chamber.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: We have to rely on evidence of factual things that are indisputable.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: In my work, whether it is professional opinion or judgement, we rely more on the Court's findings.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: So, these are factual stuff and not disputable.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: We address Members in this Chamber as hon Members.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: The public does expect us and, in particular, office holders, to have the highest integrity and honesty.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: It is, thus, not really tenable for the Leader of the Opposition to carry on in this role as it is.

speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: I rise to seek a point of clarification from the Leader of the House.

speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: First of all, I thank NMP and Senior Counsel Ms Kuah Boon Theng for sharing her experience sitting on disciplinary tribunals pursuant to the Legal Profession Act (LPA).

speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: She elaborated on the requirements for a disciplinary tribunal to find cause for disciplinary actions set out in section 83 of the LPA.

speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Arising from Nominated MP Ms Kuah's speech, I have a point of clarification to the Leader of the House.

speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Would the Leader please clarify, in general terms, how would sections 83 and/or 98 of the LPA operate where a member of the legal profession has been convicted of an offence arising from proceedings in Parliament?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Leader, you can do this in your rounding up speech.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: For nearly three years, the Speaker presided over this House, ruling on Members' conduct, maintaining order, while in an affair with a Member they presided over.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Tiong, as I recounted earlier, we can discuss about others, but you should do it with a separate Motion on another day.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: It will be relevant, Speaker, if I can just finish.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: Both Speaker and the Leader of the Opposition are Parliamentary leadership positions.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: Both situations raise questions about fitness for office.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: Arguably, the Speaker is more important than the Leader of Opposition since the Speaker is in the line of succession for President.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: Yet, Parliament was never asked to judge Mr Tan Chuan-Jin.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: Not in 2020, not in 2021, not in 2022, not before his resignation, not after.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: Nearly three years of silence and then a quiet exit, but not before calling my hon colleague an "f–ing populist".

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: No Court, no conviction, no fine, and certainly, no Motion.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Is it Mr Tiong's position that you should have fines for extramarital affairs?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: The question is about fitness for Parliamentary office and that is what this Motion is about.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: So, I believe in – let me just read the Motion again – in the third limb, you express regret that "the conduct of Mr Pritam Singh, which was dishonourable and unbecoming of a Member of Parliament".

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: So, what conditions of this situation do not obtain for Mr Tan Chuan-Jin?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Singh, you wanted to raise a point of clarification.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Yes, Mr Speaker, but not pertaining to what my colleague Mr Kenneth Tiong was saying.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Prior to this, I understand you said the Leader would be rounding up.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I just wanted to know whether there is a ruling on my —

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I wanted to hear the rest of the speeches.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I will come to my ruling very soon.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: It is regrettable that we have come to this, that the House has to discuss a Motion to express its regret at his conduct and reconsider his suitability as Leader of the Opposition.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: First, let there be no doubt that the responsibility and duty of the Leader of the Opposition sit at a high bar and rightly so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: With the privileges accorded to the office, we consider him as the foremost representative of the Opposition.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: He sits directly opposite the Prime Minister in this House, symbolising his role as a principal counterbalance to the Government of the day.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: He is accorded the right of first response in Parliament, allowing him to pose lead questions to Ministers and to speak at greater length than any other MP.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: He is also given an office in Parliament, additional staff support and resources and an allowance beyond other parliamentarians, Opposition or otherwise.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: These are privileges to enable the Leader of the Opposition to effectively lend his scrutiny to Government policy to present alternative viewpoints and to contribute meaningfully to parliamentary debate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: And at times of crises or national emergencies, as mentioned earlier, he may also receive confidential briefings by the Government.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: I think both sides of the House would agree that the office of the Leader of the Opposition comes with great responsibility, which arises out of a position of trust, trust that he would be truthful at all times, trust that he will act honourably and with integrity, and trust that when tested the strength of his character will hold firm.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: From the office of the Leader of the Opposition, Singaporeans rightly demand the highest standards to lead by example and to define the tone and tenor of how the opposition conducts itself in Parliament.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: How the Leader of the Opposition conducts himself also directly influences public's perception of our entire Parliamentary system.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Therefore, Mr Speaker, it is imperative that the Leader of the Opposition conducts himself with honour and integrity and adheres to the highest ethical standards, not only for himself, but also for the office he holds, for the Parliament he is a part of and for the people this Parliament serves.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Some may argue that this is an inordinately high bar, but it is a necessary one.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Necessary to preserve the sanctity of the proceedings in this House – Singapore's Parliament.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: As far as honesty and integrity are concerned, we must continue to be resolutely firm that there, that there is no inch at all to give and let slip in our Parliamentary and political system, regardless of which side of the House we represent.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Second, Mr Speaker, the matter before us is no longer one of doubt or conjecture.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Mr Singh has been given ample opportunity to clear the air and to defend the charges against him through due process.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: This House has devoted significant time and attention to this matter, which has been examined thoroughly over two terms of Parliament.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: The matter has been ventilated fully before the Courts and it has been conclusively determined.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: The facts have been determined and these are not matters of minor or technical significance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: An MP had lied in this Chamber when that falsehood became known.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: The Leader of the Opposition and party leader to the said MP engaged in an exercise of risk assessment or damage control, rather than opting to come clean at the first opportunity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We have a solemn duty to respect and abide by all laws of our land, act with integrity at all times and honour the trust that Singaporeans have placed in us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: To lie, to protect or conceal untruth, to even consider weighing whether an untruth would be found out fundamentally breaches the trust Singaporeans expect of us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Such conduct, Sir, I submit respectfully, is unbecoming and brings disrepute to this House.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Third, Mr Speaker, I am deeply concerned about what this episode means for the integrity of our institutions and the example we set for future generations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Younger parliamentarians and, indeed, younger Singaporeans, look to and observe the conduct of our leaders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: They look to leaders for ethical guidance and council, for standards of accountability and for direction on how integrity is upheld.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We all falter from time to time as humans inevitably do, but leadership demands prompt and honest accountability when mistakes occur.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: It therefore falls to this House to record its regret and dismay over Mr Pritam's actions, to draw a line in the sand that this is unacceptable and unbecoming, and that this cannot be what we allow within the walls of our Chamber.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Let future generations remember that this Parliament did not look away from such dishonourable conduct.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Instead, we address this matter squarely and decisively, and that we did so without hesitation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Allow me to offer three points for Parliament's consideration.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: First, the Leader of the Opposition is a role that carries significant responsibilities and duties and represents a trust that is held in high regard.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: The office is the foremost representative of the opposition.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: The Leader of the Opposition is given privileges in our parliamentary system, in terms of priority in responding to Ministers, extended time limits for his speeches, and is provided with staff support, resources and additional allowances to fulfil these responsibilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: The Leader of the Opposition sits directly opposite the Prime Minister in this House, symbolising the role of Leader of the Opposition as the principal counterbalance to the Government.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Indeed, the position of Leader of the Opposition arises out of a position of high trust specifically vested in him, including trust that he will be truthful at all times, trust that he will always act with complete honesty and integrity, and trust that in any situation, even when tested, his moral convictions, principles and personal integrity remain firm.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: In terms of honesty and integrity, we must be clear that there is absolutely no room for compromise in our parliamentary and political system, regardless of which side we represent.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Therefore, for anyone holding the position of Leader of the Opposition, Singaporeans rightly demand the highest standards of integrity and conduct to lead by example and define the tone and tenor that should be mirrored by the other opposition Members in Parliament.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Every action and the conduct of the Leader of the Opposition also directly influence public perception of our entire parliamentary system.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Therefore, it is imperative that the Leader of the Opposition conduct himself with absolute honour, not only for himself, but also to respond to the call for the integrity of the office he holds, to respect his membership in Parliament and to uphold the profound trust given by fellow citizens.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: While we may disagree in articulating policies and ideas, this must surely be based firstly on integrity and honesty.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: This is necessary in order to protect this Chamber from all falsehoods and tainted words, thereby ensuring that the sanctity and dignity of our parliamentary and political processes are preserved in the eyes of the people.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Instead, he was found to have jeopardised integrity and honour through hesitation, and at that time engaged in an exercise of risk assessment or damage control on whether or not to reveal that untruth.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We have the duty, Mr Speaker, to abide by all laws of our land, to act with integrity and honesty at all times and to honour the trust that Singaporeans have placed in us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: To lie, to delay or conceal untruth, to even consider weighing whether an untruth would be found out or not, fundamentally breaches the trust that Singaporeans expect of us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Such conduct and actions bring disrepute to the dignity, integrity and honour of this Chamber.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Third, Mr Speaker, I express concern about how this episode could affect the dignity of our institutions and the example we set for the younger generation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Younger Members of Parliament, and indeed, youth in general, closely observe and take cues from the conduct of our leaders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: They look to our leaders for ethical guidance, decisions of integrity as well as counsel, and see them as beacons in fostering a culture that underscores the importance of honesty and honour.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Although leaders may falter as humans inevitably do, it is incumbent upon leaders to take responsibility for all their actions, shortcomings and mistakes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: In this case, Mr Pritam's actions fall short.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: First, in guiding a young Member of Parliament to do the right thing when that Member of Parliament first erred.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Let us be remembered by future generations as a Parliament that did not look away, and did not shirk from our responsibility to correct misconduct and dishonesty.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: Instead, we chose to address it squarely, decisively, without any hesitation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: We must address this together so that elements that go against the identity and sacred values of Singaporeans are not allowed to even take root.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
text: With that, Mr Speaker, I lend my full support for the Motion.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Yes, Mr Speaker, I like to ask a clarification of the Member who just spoke, Dr Syed Harun.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, for the last few minutes he has been pontificating about integrity and institutions in English and Malay, in flowery language.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: If I recall correctly, in 2023, you know, he came in as an NMP and that was on the basis that he was a non-partisan person and supposed to fulfil his term as such, but he resigned prematurely and now it turns out that he was in preparation for the General Election to run as a party candidate.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I mean, does he see any issue with that in terms of integrity and institutions?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But going forward, we should not be discussing this.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But Senior Parliamentary Secretary Syed Harun, you may choose to reply.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: And I would also mention that it is a matter of public record in terms of the circumstances of what happened, with reference to what Ms Sylvia Lim mentioned.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Lim, you are free to table a separation Motion to discuss this if you wish, but not at this time.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: It is just in response to his lecture on integrity.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: And I disagree unequivocally with regard to any questions on my integrity about what has happened in the past.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: At the time when I was an NMP, very clearly, I was non-partisan.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: And at this point of time, I am quite clear in terms of my thoughts about integrity and I stand by what I have just said.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Singh, I refer to your earlier request.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Although Members enjoy certain Parliamentary privileges, we should not impinge on the mutual respect and forbearance maintained between this House and the Judiciary.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: This convention has been repeatedly upheld by this House, by me and my predecessors.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We have been in this House for over five hours.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will assume the Chair at 5.55 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended at 5.35 pm until 5.55 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Are there any other Members who wish to speak on the Motion?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is an important debate because it is about matters that affect the standing and the integrity of our Parliament.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: They have correctly pointed out that this Motion is about principles and values that we uphold.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As Dr Syed Harun and Ms Kuah Boon Theng said, the public rightfully holds high expectations of trust in our Parliament and this is even more so for the Leader of the Opposition.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling also highlighted that the quality of our Parliament embodies the values and aspirations of Singaporeans and this in turn affects how we are regarded on the global stage.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And as Mr Mark Lee pointed out, trust in our Parliament is a foundational asset for Singapore underpinning the confidence in our institutions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is good that the Opposition in Singapore has such support.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If people give you such unstinting warm support, you should not let them down.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: You should when in Parliament uphold principles of integrity and values because Singaporeans deserve a good opposition.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Singaporeans deserve an opposition who will uphold the rule of law, who will observe due process and who will respect the integrity of our institutions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But have the WP served their supporters well in the positions that you have taken today?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I, very respectfully, say the answer is no.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The position taken by the Leader of the Opposition and the WP Members who have spoken is disappointing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The sum total of their position today has really been that, you know, the rules do not apply to us and let us make a little point here.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But let us not deal with the real issue.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Let us not engage with the real fundamental point that we are talking about – which is, what kind of Parliament ought we to be.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And here let me come to the Motion.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: By and large, although the Leader of the Opposition has said that he has lifted the whip, actually, the positions do appear to be aligned across the board.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I do not think there is any real difference in the position that the WP Members have taken.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, they are able to agree to paragraphs 1 and 6 of the Motion.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Paragraph 1 affirms that honesty and integrity are fundamental pillars of Singapore's Parliamentary and political system.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, they accept that honesty and integrity are fundamental pillars of our Parliamentary and political system.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And they agree with paragraph 6, which means that they agree to call on all Members to uphold our solemn duty to respect and abide by the law and act with integrity at all times and honour the trust placed in us by Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: At the same time, however, they seem to have difficulty with the other limbs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I do not understand the difficulty in noting the High Court judgment, which basically means that we have taken due note of what the Court has found.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is troubling that WP cannot see what must surely be apparent to everyone, the inherent contradictions in their position and how much of a credibility gap there is.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: You cannot, on the one hand, say "I uphold the highest standards", then, on the other hand, say that "I have a problem saying that conduct like this is dishonourable." It is just inconsistent.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But anyway, let us examine the reasons that the WP Members have put forward for their position, and I will go through them one by one.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, the first point is Mr Singh basically is saying that he disagrees with the High Court decision over the Court decisions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We know that the Courts have found Mr Singh guilty on two counts of lying to the COP and they made other findings, which I referred to in my earlier speech.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: After the High Court decision, Mr Singh said, "I respect and accept the judgment fully and without reservation".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On the face of it, accepting the judgment should mean that he accepts the verdict but, of course, Mr Singh now tells us that that is not the case.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In fact, he had an issue because he said that I did not highlight what he said earlier about the judgment also, because at that same interview, he had said that the verdict was disappointing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I looked very carefully at the media statement.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He said it was disappointing, and then he went on to say – let me just look at that.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He went on to say that, "I have always had deep respect for the independence, rigour and professionalism of the Courts." He said that while he was disappointed with the verdict, he respected and accepted the judgment fully and without reservation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And when Mr Singh says something, the question is, what are we to understand of it?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And we have seen what the Courts understood of it, and we have seen what the Courts ruled that Ms Khan understood of it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We have also seen what the COP understood of it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, fundamentally, despite the fact that he has had the full opportunity to canvass his case, he is basically saying that he does not accept the Court judgment.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is strange because when the COP Report was brought to Parliament, Mr Singh vehemently disputed it at that time – and do not forget that this is a COP that has sat on it – and Mr Singh has come to this Parliament, today, to say, as he has said many times, Parliament is supreme.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: When you have a Select Committee of Parliament that makes a finding, it should be supreme.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If the finding affects Mr Singh, it is not supreme.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And at that time, we agreed to refer it to the PP, basically to allow him the benefit of canvassing his case in full, and so that we would have the benefit of a full finding so that it could not be said that this Parliament somehow, unilaterally made a decision based purely on the findings of the COP.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And Mr Singh had the opportunity to – well, firstly, the PP looked at it, took an independent view and found that on the face of it, charges were made out.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The District Court had the benefit of seeing witnesses, hearing evidence, Mr Singh had the benefit of counsel.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Basically, what Mr Singh is saying today is that "Despite all of this, despite the fact that I had the fullest opportunity, every opportunity, to contest this and bring evidence, they are wrong." I accept that Mr Singh may not agree with it, but the point is this.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And when there are disputes, somebody has to decide, because if one person says A and another person says B, who do you believe?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And that is the reason why you have Courts.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is the reason why you have Courts as a neutral and independent arbiter, with the opportunity for parties to bring the evidence and set out their case, and then the Court decides.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And so, here we are today, with a Court judgment basically having found Mr Singh guilty of lying and we are being asked to note this.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And in the light of this, how do we say that such conduct is acceptable?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, when each of us go internationally and we are asked, "Oh, your Leader of the Opposition, he has been convicted for lying twice.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Is that okay?" And our answer should be, "Oh yes, it is okay, because he says he is right.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: A Court judgment does not matter." How would people regard Singapore in that situation?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is not about Mr Singh per se.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is about the fact that his conduct has been adjudicated on by the Courts.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There is the District Court finding that he had guided Ms Khan to lie, and we have the COP Report – do not forget, Parliament is supreme – which has found that he had lied.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, what are we to do in those circumstances?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, I have to say that the first point that Mr Singh has made is not really persuasive, and it does not answer the Motion.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I come now to the second part of what he said.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Singh said that what he does accept is that he was guilty of taking too long to respond to Ms Khan's lie in Parliament.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He had mentioned that in his media interview.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But that actually is not the crux of the Court finding because the Court did not find that he was liable because he took too long.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In fact, the reasons that he gave for taking too long, in other words, allowing Ms Khan to go and speak to her parents and so on, the Court actually did not accept.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And let me read what the Court had said.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The High Court essentially did not accept Mr Singh's account of that.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He said, "A person's reaction or inaction to significant events is usually revealing of his or her understanding of the events.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If indeed, if it was the appellant's view that Ms Khan should, at some point, clarify the untruth, one would expect that steps would have been taken to decide what, when and how such clarification should be made.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The telling of the Untruth was a significant event for the WP, given the potentially serious political fallout if it were not properly managed.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Yet, it is common ground that between the 8 August meeting and the 3 October Meeting, nothing was said between the appellant and Ms Khan or among the WP leaders about making preparations for a clarification of the Untruth.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The complete absence of any discussion during this period is entirely consistent with Ms Khan's evidence, that at the 8 August Meeting, the appellant had told her to take the Untruth to the grave, where the upshot of the Grave Statement was that nothing further needed to be done about the Untruth.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The appellant's complete inaction between the 8 August Meeting and the 3 October Meeting stands in stark contrast with the appellant's involvement in drafting Ms Khan's personal statement between 15 and 30 October 2021, following the meeting with Mr Low on 11 October", and so on.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Court did not say that it was a matter of just "delay".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Court found that the explanation for "delay" was not believable and rejected it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That was what led the Court to believe, amongst other things, that the statement had, in fact, been made.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then, I come to Ms Lim's point, where Ms Lim argues that basically she has not been charged in Court; this does not really affect her and is not relevant to her.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I go back to the terms of the Motion.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: All I am asking here is to ask the House to note that the High Court judgment and the Committee's findings have implications for Ms Lim and Mr Faisal, which have to be considered separately.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I had actually in my earlier speech explained the linkage.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It would have been clear from my reading of the Court judgment but let me just connect the dots for everyone.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: When the COP Report came out, there were two things in relation to Ms Lim and Mr Faisal.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: One was that she had lied to the COP that the statement to "take it to the grave" was never said, that that did not happen.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, one count was for lying to the COP.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The other was for her involvement in guiding Ms Raeesah Khan to hide the Untruth.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because if you tell somebody or if you agree with "taking it to the grave", you are basically guiding somebody to keep it quiet.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In other words, there are two outstanding things.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Of course, Ms Lim had disputed the COP findings.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Therefore, it must follow from there that the Court findings are actually consistent with the COP Report.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because what is before Parliament – which had been deferred – is the COP Report, which found that she lied and had been involved in guiding Ms Khan.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And we said, wait until the outcome of the case.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then, you look at the case and the Court has looked at it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Court says, yes, the meeting took place, they were both there, that Statement was made.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is why the Court judgment has implications.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As to what we should do with regard to Ms Lim, that is something that should be dealt with separately.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Speaker has already indicated that if you are making assertions or if you are dealing with a particular Member, that should be the subject matter of a separate Motion.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But I just wanted to make sure that in this Motion, that we note that and we will come back.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Giam had asked whether this would take a very long time.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But today, we wanted to deal with a specific topic.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I hope that addresses the issues with regard to the limb.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because it has implications for Ms Lim and Mr Faisal.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: With respect to Mr Faisal, there was a bit of an attempt to muddy the waters here, because it was said that the Police have already issued an Advisory to Mr Faisal and therefore, the matter should be considered close.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But Mr Faisal was referred to the PP for a different matter.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: One, when he was before the COP, he had flat out refused to answer some of their queries.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For that, he was referred to the PP.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But the second two we agreed to defer, pending the outcome of Mr Singh's case.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And for the same reasons as for Ms Lim, it has implications, because Mr Faisal was present at that meeting too.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In the COP hearing, he had denied that such a statement was made.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Ms Lim and I think Mr Giam have attempted to suggest that this is political punishment, that Mr Singh is being punished twice.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: When you have a Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of a company and, let us say, he has been charged and convicted of a matter of a crime of dishonesty, how many companies actually say, "Yes, it is okay, Mr CEO, please continue"?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: How does that look to other people outside?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: How can we then say that for someone to whom this has happened, is suitable to continue as the Leader of the Opposition?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For the PAP side of the House, we say it is very difficult.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But somehow, the WP does not seem to have a difficulty with this, which tells us something about the WP's values.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then, Mr Kenneth Tiong raised the question of Mr Tan Chuan-Jin and asked, oh, nothing happened there; why is that the case that it was alright there and not here?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I am frankly very disappointed in that stance.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But it also shows that Mr Tiong does not quite understand the issue.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Initially, if you read the Hansard carefully, then Prime Minister has said it was clear in his mind he would have had to step down as Speaker.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He wanted to give him some time to settle constituency matters, settle family matters, but it was clear that as Speaker, he would have had to step down.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Whether they should resign their seats, initially, that was something to be thought about.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But when it became clear that the conduct had not stopped, then Prime Minister said, you must step down, and Ms Cheng had to step down too.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I believe he had apologised to Singaporeans that it had happened.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Here, Mr Singh is not even being asked to resign his seat – at least, not by us.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And he does not seem to think that there is a problem with continuing as the Leader of the Opposition.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There is no equivalence at all in those examples.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, that is with respect to section 94 of the Legal Profession Act.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We have to ask ourselves about the reasons that have been put forward by the WP.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And having examined them, they do not hold water.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We really do have to look at how the WP had dealt with Ms Raeesah Khan before and Mr Leon Perera.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In the case of Ms Khan, she was told she had to resign within 24 hours, otherwise she would be expelled.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Or rather, she would be expelled within 24 hours if she did not resign.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Somehow, in Ms Khan's case, lying was suddenly a very serious offence for the WP.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In Mr Leon Perera's case, he also had to step down because he had lied to the WP leadership, so it was very serious there.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But somehow, for the WP, when you have a case of their leader lying to the COP – and under oath at that – they seem to regard it differently.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The only possible conclusion when you compare this and the previous cases with Ms Khan and Mr Perera is that in those cases, the WP has made a political calculation as to whether those Members should be kept or not.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Perera was dropped like a hot potato.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But they have made or appear to have made a political calculation with respect to Mr Singh and then, hope maybe over time, people will forget – instead of taking a principled stance on their party leaders' conduct, which could be politically costly.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, Ms Khan and Mr Perera were expendable.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is why in today's Motion, we have been hearing the equivocating and the temporising and the avoiding, of doing what they must know in their heart of hearts is the right thing to do.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But that is not leadership, nor is it responsibility.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is not what Singaporeans expect of political leaders and parties.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is not the way to build a First World Parliament or even a two-party system.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is not the way to build a party that aspires to offer an alternative government to Singaporeans one day.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The WP MPs must surely know this, but they are all going along with the party line.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is not good for the Opposition cause.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: At the end of the day, we have a scenario where Mr Singh says he respects and accepts the judgment, but does not agree with it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The WP talks about the rule of law, but they set themselves above it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The WP calls for accountability, but they will not call their own member to account.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I hope the WP will remember that every time they stand up in Parliament, from this day onwards and speak about accountability, they will be reminded of their standard of accountability.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And every time they stand in Parliament and tell us about the rule of law and how we must abide by it, we will remind them how they have abided by the rule of law today.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We now have a much clearer idea of what the WP stands for, which is simply that the rules and the law apply to everyone else but not to them.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But Mr Speaker, this cannot be the standard that we set for our Parliament.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We have a duty to Singaporeans and to Singapore to ensure that the high standards are maintained.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We cannot endorse dishonourable conduct or ignore the Court judgment.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And we cannot talk about a First World Parliament and effective checks and balances when fundamental values of honesty, integrity and accountability are not upheld.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As MPs, we have a solemn duty to make sure that politics in Singapore remains upright and honourable.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If Members care about this, then I urge Members to support the Motion.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I took some notes as the Leader was speaking.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: If I got some of her representations wrong, please let me know.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The Leader said that the WP's position seems to be that the rules do not apply to us.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I do not believe this was the position anyone made.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But in the course of her speech, she also mentioned somebody has to decide.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I fully accept the authority and the finality of the Court's decision.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: It does not require a person to abandon their honest belief about their motivations and their values.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: It has been one month since the judgment.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And I will continue to do my work faithfully, as I have done for the last 15 years.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: On the point that the Leader made, I think towards the end of her round up speech, where she gave us advice on what is good for the WP and good for the Opposition.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I think we can be the judge of that, with due respect.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: We have always championed the importance of a rational, responsible, respectable Opposition in the House and will continue to do so.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: In terms of this point, the Opposition exists not because it is infallible, but because democratic systems, particularly one-party dominant systems, require challenge, require balance and genuine alternative voices.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And as long as this role is performed lawfully, respectfully, it remains legitimate and important.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And the WP will continue serving in this role.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: That is all I have to say, Mr Speaker, with regard to clarifications.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I had a clarification for the Leader, which she has not replied, about the number of briefings that were given to me, the number of trips I went to, which was a point she made.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, I think she should close the loop on that.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The point about the Leader of the Opposition role is that it gets certain specific privileges, and that was one of them.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And that was the point I was making.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then, the other point that Mr Singh had made about the WP being a judge of their own cause.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I think that is exactly what we have seen today.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He has been a judge in his own cause.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And the other point that he made was that the Opposition was not infallible.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I did not say I was a judge in my own cause.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: As I mentioned, the respected President who opened this House takes a view about a criminal conviction.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But that does not mean I disrespect the Courts.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: With respect to him, it was a matter of negligence.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And the point really is, that in this case, you have a Court judgment.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Singh has said that he disagrees with it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He may do so, but that does not mean that the Court findings should not be noted.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That does not mean that the conduct that was found in the Court judgments should not be regarded as dishonourable or unbecoming.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But the question is when something goes wrong, what do you do?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And at that crossroads of doing right and wrong, if you take one direction, it goes a certain path, and if you take another direction, it goes another path.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And as I mentioned earlier, in the case of Ms Khan, she was led along a certain path, with the consequences that we see today.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And the other point he made was that what is important is that we perform our role lawfully.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And that is the point, is it not?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because lying before the COP cannot be said to be performing that role lawfully.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The first is that she mentioned more than once that the WP was somehow being inconsistent, in the sense that in Ms Raeesah Khan's case and also Mr Leon Perera's case, we seem to have acted very swiftly.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But in this case, Mr Singh has contested the charges and still maintains his innocence today.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, WP is acting on the judgment, as she noted, we have formed a DP to look into whether Mr Singh has contravened the constitution.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And although she says that she cannot wait for us – that is fine.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But the fact is that we have our processes and the processes will take their course.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The other clarification which I wish to make was in relation to Resolution 5.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: She mentioned that the Court has found that certain statements were made in the August 2021 meeting, and that is a fact.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But as I had said earlier, neither Mr Faisal nor myself were involved in the trial, we did not give evidence.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, in that sense, of course, the Court made its finding based on the evidence before it.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But the fact is that we did not have the opportunity to give our recollection to the Court.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I am still going to maintain that those findings cannot be held against me, and perhaps, at the next phase, or whenever it is, I will take this up again.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, you have a COP Report where that finding is there.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: What today's Motion does is it refers to the Court finding, because you see, the point is simply this: did the meeting happen and were the words said?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Those words were said, found all three of them were present.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The COP Report is a report which, according to Mr Singh, should be a supreme document.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Singh did not say that the document is supreme.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He said Parliament is supreme, and I am talking —

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And this sovereign Parliament has a Select Committee that has made a report from a Committee of Privileges, finding that Mr Singh had made the statement, that Ms Lim and Mr Faisal were there, and that they had lied to the COP.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The question on everybody's minds is: "Well, Mr Singh's case is going to Court.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Let the Court make its findings, then we have the benefit of that.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And we find that the Court findings are pretty much the same as the COP's findings —

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On the point of that meeting occurred and the statement having been made.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, that being the case, it has implications because we could have proceeded back when the original Report was made, we could have proceeded at the time.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But what you have is where the Court findings have confirmed that the meeting took place and the statement was made.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is all that this Motion does: to note that it has implications.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But Ms Lim may want to take that up the next time when the next Motion comes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And with respect to the point about the difference between Ms Khan's and Mr Perera's case, Ms Lim said that the difference was that, in their case, they admitted their wrongdoing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is a really interesting point, because that means that everybody who goes to Court and who basically, puts up a defence and is found guilty, so long as they did not admit, it means that they are not guilty.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But what kind of rule of law is that?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: You cannot go simply on the basis of, "Has the person admitted or not?" Here you have a system, where you have a society, you have a Court system.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Court makes an adjudication, and as Parliament, we have to take note of that and act accordingly.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I raised my hand for Point of Order and the Leader corrected herself.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Just to follow up on the Leader's point that as I mentioned in my clarification, the WP is looking into whether Mr Singh has contravened the constitution.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I have a point of clarification for the Leader of the House.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In her round-up speech, she made the assertion, and please correct me if I am wrong, that the voting patterns of the WP's MPs will, in some way indicate that we find ourselves above the rule of law, that we do not agree with the rule of law, or we find ourselves above the law.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The rule of law implies that we respect the independence of the Courts and their role as an independent arbiter in disputes.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And once an adjudication is made and a ruling is passed, we respect it and we abide by it.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is in the interest of order; and if not, we will have anarchy.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: That does not preclude us from disagreeing with their verdicts and that does not mean that if we disagree, we are above the rule of law.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I just wondered how he was able to disagree with it, when he was not a witness or a party to the Court proceedings.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
text: I did not make the point that I personally disagree with the ruling.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
text: As Ms Lim mentioned, the WP has our own processes.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
text: My point is that the Leader has made the assertion that, based on the way we are going to vote on this Motion, that that would imply that the WP sees themselves as above the law.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Perhaps Mr Low could just clarify what his position is on all six limbs of the Motion?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Any other clarifications for the Leader of the House?
The question is, "That this Parliament — 1.
Affirms that honesty and integrity are fundamental pillars of Singapore’s parliamentary and political system; 2.

Notes the judgment in Pritam Singh v Public Prosecutor   SGHC 242 where the High Court upheld Mr Pritam Singh’s conviction for lying to the Committee of Privileges, and the findings of the Committee of Privileges that he had guided Ms Raeesah Khan to continue with her lie to Parliament; 3.
Expresses regret at the conduct of Mr Pritam Singh, which was dishonourable and unbecoming of a Member of Parliament; 4.
Notes that the High Court judgment and the Committee’s findings have implications for Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap, which have to be considered separately; and 6.

Calls upon all Members of Parliament to uphold their solemn duty to respect and abide by the law, act with integrity at all times, and honour the trust placed in them by Singaporeans." Those who agree, say "Aye".

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Can I request that whichever WP MP wishes, they may have their dissent recorded?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Can I request that those who would like their dissent to be recorded, to kindly stand?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I think the "Ayes" have it, the "Ayes" have it.
